problem:
A function $g(x)$ has values according to the table below:

| $x$ | $0$ | $0.3$ | $0.6$ | $0.9$ | $1.2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $g(x)$ | $-2.7$ | $-1.6$ | $-0.4$ | $1.1$ | $3.7$ |

Approximate ${g}^{′}(x)$ at the point $x=0.6$ using a forward difference approximation. Do not round the answer.

${g}^{′}(0.6)≈$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
We use the forward difference approximation

$$
{g}^{′}(x)≈\frac{g(x+h)-g(x)}{h}
$$

at the point $x=0.6.$ We choose the step size $h$ to be as small as possible, in this case $h=0.3.$ This gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(0.6) & ≈\frac{g(0.6+0.3)-g(0.6)}{0.3} \\  & =\frac{g(0.9)-g(0.6)}{0.3} \\  & =\frac{1.1-(-0.4)}{0.3} \\  & =\frac{1.5}{0.3} \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$
